author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
The risk of a conflict over Taiwan is shaping Japanese defence planning, with Tokyo shoring up security at home and abroad for a potentially prolonged fight. But there are economic, demographic and political constraints on how far its military transformation can go. In the first of a three-part series, Gabriel Dominguez examines how Japan is building a network of partnerships to strengthen its strategic endurance.
Japan is rapidly building a web of defence partnerships spanning the Indo-Pacific...
title: How Tokyo is widening regional defence ties to complicate Beijing’s Taiwan calculus

author: Fan Chen
description:
His summit with Donald Trump is just over two weeks away, but already this month Xi Jinping has had one of his busiest stretches of diplomatic travel in recent years.
First he wrapped up the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, and then he made a state visit to Egypt.
Xi is expected to head off again later this week to visit New Delhi for the Brics summit before he travels to Washington. Beijing has not yet confirmed those two trips, in line with its practice of...
title: As clock counts down to Trump summit, Xi boosts global clout with diplomatic blitz

author: Dannie Peng
description:
Chinese cities must brace for a potential nuclear attack, a new study has warned, singling out Japan for “sending a major danger signal” to the world.
The report, from a People’s Liberation Army medical team, said the likelihood of a large-scale global nuclear war was relatively low.
“However, the possibility cannot be ruled out that small or medium-sized nuclear-armed or potentially nuclear-armed states, driven by geopolitical or religious conflicts, could carry out a single nuclear-weapon...
title: PLA Rocket Force highlights ‘major danger signal’ from Japan in nuclear terror study

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Authorities in central China have joined forces to investigate suspected industrial dumping on the Yangtze River following the release of rare drone footage of the activity.
The environment bureau in the Hubei city of Wuhan said on Monday that it had launched the inquiry in association with police and transport authorities.
The announcement comes less than two weeks after Beijing revised performance assessment rules for officials, holding them accountable for life for serious environmental...
title: Rare drone film of suspected dumping spurs Chinese agencies into investigation

author: Shi Jiangtao
description:
Chinese Premier Li Qiang pledged to deepen cooperation with Qatar in energy, investment, AI and diplomatic efforts to de-escalate Middle East tensions.
Li delivered the remarks during a meeting on Monday in Beijing with Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who is on an official two-day visit to China aimed at bolstering bilateral ties.
His visit came as Beijing and Doha sought to navigate an increasingly volatile regional security environment and...
title: China vows deeper cooperation with Qatar in energy, AI and Middle East de-escalation

author: Victoria Bela
description:
China and Russia have conducted their first joint on-site sea ice survey in the Arctic Ocean aboard the Xuelong 2 research icebreaker, as tensions continue to rise over economic opportunities in the rapidly warming northern region.
Two researchers from Russia’s Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute boarded Xuelong 2 as part of China’s 16th Arctic Ocean Expedition, according to a report by state broadcaster CCTV on Saturday.
According to Lin Long, captain of the Xuelong 2 sea ice team, this...
title: China and Russia launch first sea ice survey aboard Xuelong 2 as Arctic tensions swell

author: Carol Yang
description:
Relations between China and Mexico should not be influenced by outside powers, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Monday, following reports the United States was pressuring its neighbour over its ties to Beijing.
“China-Mexico relations are not directed at any third party, nor should they be influenced by any third party,” Wang told his Mexican counterpart Roberto Velasco Alvarez.
He added that China supported Mexico in maintaining its independence, safeguarding its sovereignty and security and...
title: China warns against ‘third party’ interference after reports of US pressure on Mexico

author: James David Spellman
description:
The “circular deals” among AI titans increasingly resemble the “daisy chains” of the 1980s savings-and-loan crisis.
Forty years ago, interconnected transactions obscured the dangers, multiplied systemic risks and helped inflate asset values before roughly a third of US thrift banks failed. Today’s financial engineering – an incestuous ecosystem of interlocking multi-year commitments to provide financing, buy semiconductors, secure gigawatts of power and lease data centres – could meet a similar...
title: AI titans’ ‘circular deals’ are starting to look like ‘daisy chains’

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan’s military plans to step up its cyber defences against mainland China with a new threat-hunting team and foreign expertise as it deepens cooperation with the US.
The Information, Communications and Electronic Force Command has earmarked NT$95.93 million (US$3.03 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to establish the team and bring foreign experts and instructors to Taiwan for advanced training.
According to the budget plan, which still needs legislative approval, the programme would focus...
title: Taiwan sets up US-backed cyber unit to hunt hidden military threats

author: Alcott Wei
description:
A television drama produced by Beijing’s top counter-espionage agency has put the spotlight on real-life cases in the high-stakes intelligence battle between mainland China and Taiwan.
Over the past decade, mainland Chinese spy dramas have rarely touched on contemporary espionage across the Taiwan Strait but on Sunday state broadcaster CCTV began airing a 40-episode television series about such intelligence efforts from 1998 to 2018.
Overseen by the Ministry of State Security, The Long Watch...
title: Rare Beijing spy series highlights real-life intelligence drama with Taiwan

author: Chao Kong
description:
US President Donald Trump’s vision of new warships bristling with huge-calibre guns – widely mocked as a billionaire’s vanity project and a throwback to the battleship era of the second world war – has received an unexpected nod from military scientists in China.
In a paper published last month by the Chinese peer-reviewed journal Command Control & Simulation, the authors suggested that large-calibre naval guns could have a critical role in future warfare by countering the growing threat of...
title: Chinese naval scientists fall in love with the ‘big guns’ on Trump-class warship

author: Dulue Mbachu
description:
Cost appears to be a deciding factor for most African countries when it comes to energy as they observe the factors that influence US and Chinese policy decisions.
In a sign of the contrasting energy strategies pursued by Washington and Beijing, US President Donald Trump says “drill, baby, drill” while China drives a leap towards renewable energy.
With China’s advances in solar generation and battery technologies making acquisitions cheaper, a consensus is coalescing across the continent around...
title: How China’s green tech is undercutting Trump’s ‘drill, baby, drill’ oil strategy in Africa

author: Carol Yang
description:
Fresh off Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Kyrgyzstan, project officials have announced the successful drilling of a key tunnel along the long-stalled China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan (CKU) railway.
This marks the first milestone for the flagship project under Beijing’s Belt and Road Initiative, offering China a critical trade corridor bypassing Russia.
The 210-metre (690-foot) tunnel was the first drilled through in the Kyrgyz section since full-scale work began in June 2025, China’s state...
title: China marks major tunnel milestone for Central Asia railway bypassing Russia
